lawyer:
Dr Md Zahir with Shah Md Ezaz Rahman, Advocates—For the Petitioners. 
Akhtar Imam with MM Nuruzzaman, Advocates—For Respondent Nos. 1-3. 
M Moniruzzaman Khan with Morshed Ahmed Khan and ASM Abdur Razzaque, Advocates—For Respondent No. 6.
parties:
Anwar Hossain (Md) & another ------ Petitioners 
Vs 
Uttara Valley Ltd and other ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 3. The respondent Nos. 1-3 in their affidavit-in-opposition stated, amongst others, that the lands were purchased in the name of the respondent-company for setting up poultry, apiculture and agriculture farms, through registered sale deeds, and that the petitioner No. 1, Managing Director of the Company, is in control of the management, affairs and business of the Company and that the land in question has been purchased by the respondent No. 6, a reputed physician and also the Managing Partner of the Partnership Firm namely, Nurjahan Poly Clinic and General Hospital at Sylhet, and that land was purchased for setting up a Modern Charitable Hospital and that Board of Directors of the Company decided to sell the company land to the respondent Nos. 6-8 and the Board resolution was taken in presence of the petitioner No. 1 and that the resolution books are in the custody of the petitioner No. 1 and that the consideration money against the sale of the land was duly paid to respondent-company with which the income tax and land development tax were paid and costs of construction of boundary wall around the Company's land was met and the petitioner No.1 also utilised money out of the sale proceeds of the land and that the petitioner No.1 earlier sold valuable trees from the company's land valued around Taka 20,00,000 which amount was not credited in the account of the company and that the petitioner No.1 submitted his objection in the mutation case on 10-12-02 and 12-12-02 and the respondent No. 9, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Sylhet Sadar, asked the petitioner No.1 to produce Company's resolution book and the petitioner No. 1 took time up to 19-1-03 for compliance and that the petitioner No.1 removed all the records of the Company and has fabricated new records, which he fraudulently submitted to the office of the Registrar, Joint Stock Companies and Firms on 17-12-02 and took back those on 19-12-02, against which the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 submitted objection petition and the petitioner No.1 accordingly was asked to submit the relevant papers and documents vide memo No. 155 dated 1-2-03 and memo No. 450 dated 17-3-03 but the petitioner No. 1 till date did not comply and that the petitioner filed an affidavit dated 19-8-03 stating that he did not have any document, which he was asked to produce by .Court's order dated 17-3-03 and that the sale proceeds of 16.26 acres of land, evidenced by Annexures F-I (5) to the application, were shared by Mina Uddin and others and as well as the respondent-company (Uttara Valley Limited) and that Minauddin and others received Taka 3,70,000 and the respondent-company received Taka 3,00,000, with which the Company paid income tax and land development tax and that the petitioner No. 1 himself executed two sale deeds in respect of land sold by the Company in favour of one Abdul Hamid Chowdhury and one Lokman Hakim for Taka 60,000, which amount he did not deposit in the Company's account and that Miner Uddin and Sayma, co-owners of the land in the same khatian sold together with Company's land, and they appointed the respondent No. 3 as their attorney to execute and register the impugned sale deeds on their behalf and that the respondent No. 3 was authorised to sell land of the Company by the same resolution, by which the petitioner No. 1 was authorised to execute and register the sale deeds in favour of said Abdul Hamid Chowdhury and Lokman Hakim, and that the resolution book containing the said resolution is in custody of the petitioner No. 1 and that the petitioner No. 1 has filed this petition malafide, inasmuch as the petitioner No. 1 as Managing Director was the Chief Executive of the Company at the relevant time and he was in the management of the Company and, as such, he was in custody of all the books and records of the Company and that on the land sold a Charitable Hospital is to be constructed and that no meeting of the Board of Directors was held on 25-11-97 and 20-11-02 to appoint Managing Director of the Company and that there is no evidence as alleged that any fraud has been practiced on the minority shareholder or that the affairs of the Company were being managed in a manner prejudicial to the interest of the members or to the exclusion of the petitioner No.1; and that in view of the existing provisions of the Articles of Association of the Company there is no necessity for passing an order by this Court further empowering the Managing Director to participate in the management of the Company and that the office of the Company was used by the petitioner No.1 for his Travel Agency business during the period 1994-2002 AD; and that the petitioner No.1 and his son were responsible for filing false case against the respondent No. 3, which was dismissed being found to be false and baseless on investigation, and that there is no necessity for amending the powers of the Executive Director of the respondent-company by amendment of Article 82 of the Articles of Association of the respondent-company, as prayed for, and that there being disputed questions of fact as to the genuineness and or forgery of the documents, the resolution of the Board of Directors and others and as those cannot be resolved in a summary proceeding, and need be decided by taking evidences in appropriate civil suit, the instant application under section 233 of the Companies Act, 1994, is not maintainable and that this Company Court cannot and will not cancel the registered sale deeds in an application under section 233 of the Companies Act and that the petition is also not maintainable on the ground that it will affect the right, title and interest of the innocent 3rd party, who are bonafide purchasers; and that the transaction complained of is an isolated transaction of the Company and there being no continuity of the allegation complained of at the time of filing of the instant application, the application under section 233 of the Companies Act is not maintainable.
